title: The optimal randomized-versus-quantum query exponent for total Boolean functions
exact_target: For bounded-error query complexities of total Boolean functions, is the smallest universal polynomial exponent exactly four: $R(f)=O((1+Q(f))^4)$ for every f, while for every fixed $k\geq 2$ there are total functions $F_{k,m}$, along sufficiently large powers of four m, with $Q\leq C_k$ sqrt(m)(log $m)^{b_k}$ and $R\geq c_k$ $m^{2-1/k}/(\log $ $m)^2$?
